title: calque configuration
description: Configuration for calque, which generates ORM code from orm-annotated .proto files for one or more target languages and storage backends. Point an editor at this with a modeline: # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heojeongbo/calque/main/calque.schema.json

version.description: The config format version. Required, so that a future format change reports itself instead of producing a cascade of errors about keys that were valid in the version you wrote.

targets.description: What to generate. Each entry pairs a language target with a storage backend. Two entries may name the same target, if one of them is given a distinct `name`.

target.description: A target registered in the calque binary being run, and the key of that target's own top-level options section.

backend.description: A storage backend registered in the calque binary being run. The target must support it: pairing a language with a store its runtime has no adapter for is refused at generate time, not discovered at import time. Required for every target but a storeless one -- output that describes no store takes no backend, and naming one for it is an error. Which targets are storeless depends on the binary, so this schema cannot require it and calque checks instead.

out.description: A subdirectory of the output root buf gives the plugin. Not an output root of its own -- buf owns that. An absolute path, or one containing '..', is refused.

name.description: Disambiguates two entries with the same target. Defaults to the target name. It is a label rather than a section key: options are claimed under the target's own name, so two entries running the same target read the same options.

$comment: The top level is deliberately open: every target and backend claims a section named after itself, and this schema cannot know which ones a given calque binary registers. calque itself rejects any top-level section nothing claimed, so a misspelled section name is still loud -- it just fails at generate time rather than in the editor.
